prompt: A Philippine Army brigade commander wants a combined arms force that fights mounted and uses armor-protected vehicles as its principal means of accomplishing a ground combat mission. Which force fits this description?
options: Armor
A dismounted light infantry force
A towed field artillery battery
A static fire-support cell
explanation: Page 13 defines armor as a combined arms force designed for mounted combat using armor-protected vehicles.

prompt: A battalion S3 briefs that armor operations should climax in a powerful, violent action at the decisive time and place. Which statement matches how the lesson says this is achieved?
options: Fire and maneuver are combined and controlled to create a preponderance of combat power
Maneuver alone is used because firing would reveal friendly positions to the enemy
Combat power is spread evenly across the front so no sector is weak at any time
Contact is avoided until the enemy has exhausted its own combat power in defense
explanation: Page 13 says armor operations are conducted by fire and maneuver, combined and controlled to create a preponderance of combat power.

prompt: An armor battalion drafts the doctrinal mission statement for its operations order. Which wording does the Armor Operations manual give?
options: To close with and neutralize enemy forces by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other arms
To hold terrain with static fires and avoid close combat with enemy forces during the operation
To destroy enemy forces only by indirect fire delivered from standoff positions behind the main body
To provide area security for rear installations without engaging the enemy forces directly
explanation: Page 14 states the doctrinal mission of armor.

prompt: After an ambush, a company commander praises his armored vehicles for shielding the crews from small arms fire. Which characteristic of armor is he describing?
options: Shock action
Mobility
Flexibility
Armor protection
explanation: Page 20 lists armor protection as the first characteristic of armor.

prompt: A staff officer lists the characteristics of armor for a class. Which item does NOT appear among the characteristics in the lesson?
options: Amphibious landing capability
Armor protection
Mobility
Shock action
explanation: Page 20 lists armor protection, firepower, mobility, flexibility, intensive and flexible communication, and shock action.

prompt: A battalion commander asks what a mechanized infantry unit is expected to do. Which mission does the lesson give?
options: Perform reconnaissance and surveillance and provide security for the unit it is assigned to
Close with the enemy by fire and maneuver to destroy or capture him, or repel his assault by fire, close combat and counterattack
Neutralize the enemy by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other arms
Provide indirect fire support to the main body from covered positions behind the line
explanation: Pages 18 and 23 give the mechanized infantry mission; the distractors are the cavalry and tank missions.

prompt: A new platoon leader asks how his mechanized infantry platoon is equipped and organized. Which description matches the lesson?
options: Three AIFVs; a platoon headquarters and two squads, with the platoon leader riding in a truck
Four AIFVs, each carrying a complete platoon headquarters and one squad of the company
Two AIFVs; a platoon headquarters and four squads, with the squads sharing the vehicles
Four AIFVs; a platoon headquarters and three squads, with the platoon leader and HQ in one AIFV
explanation: Page 27 describes the platoon organization and how the platoon rides in its four AIFVs.

prompt: In a mechanized infantry squad, a student asks who makes up the carrier team. Which answer is correct?
options: The squad leader, the automatic rifleman and the grenadier
The carrier team leader, the gunner and the driver
The gunner, the driver and the platoon leader
All squad members who are not part of the vehicle crew
explanation: Page 26 says the carrier team is the carrier team leader, gunner and driver; the dismount team is everyone else in the squad.

prompt: A mechanized infantry platoon is fighting mounted in its AIFVs. Which task is a mounted capability in the lesson?
options: Infiltrate enemy positions
Destroy light armored vehicles
Move over terrain not trafficable by vehicles
Secure obstacles to defeat enemy breaching efforts
explanation: Page 28 lists mounted capabilities; the other options are dismounted capabilities from page 29.

prompt: A platoon leader must move through a swamp trail that AIFVs cannot use and infiltrate an enemy position. Which employment and reason fit the lesson?
options: Mounted, because AIFVs cross any terrain the infantry can cross and infiltrate positions
Mounted, because dismounted infantry are unable to infiltrate enemy positions at all
Neither; infiltration of enemy positions is a task reserved for tank units only
Dismounted, because infantry can move over terrain vehicles cannot and can infiltrate positions
explanation: Page 29 lists infiltrating enemy positions and moving over terrain not trafficable by vehicles as dismounted capabilities.

prompt: A squad dismounts in the open and takes casualties from enemy mortars. Which stated limitation best explains this?
options: AVs are restricted to certain avenues of approach due to terrain limitations
Infantrymen need sufficient time to mount and dismount their vehicles
AIFVs and APCs are more vulnerable than tanks to anti-armor weapons
Dismounted infantrymen are vulnerable to small arms and indirect fire
explanation: Page 30 lists that dismounted infantrymen are vulnerable to small arms and indirect fire.

prompt: A squad is about to dismount from its AIFV. Which dismounting SOP is correct?
options: Weapons are carried with the chamber empty and the muzzle down
Soldiers take cover behind the AV once they are out of the vehicle
Soldiers ride on top of the AV between positions to save time
The first soldier to dismount is also the first to mount again
explanation: Page 31 lists chamber empty, muzzle down; never hide behind an AV; no riders on top; first to dismount is last to mount.

prompt: A squad dismounts left and comes under fire from the right. Which objectives apply after the dismount?
options: Remain mounted and let the AIFV absorb the fire until the enemy withdraws from the area
React to the contact on the right, extricate out of the kill zone, then perform IAD after dismount procedures
Dismount right toward the enemy to close with it at once, without any reaction drill
Wait at the door of the AV for the enemy fire to stop before taking any action
explanation: Pages 35-39 give the objectives for dismounting left under fire from the right.

prompt: After a patrol, a squad boards its AIFV. Which mounting SOP applies?
options: All soldiers rush the door together so the squad is inside as quickly as possible
Keep weapons loaded with muzzles up once inside the AV to stay ready
Provide cover while others mount, and move inside one at a time without piling at the door
The last soldier to dismount boards first so he can sit nearest the door
explanation: Page 45 lists the mounting SOPs.

prompt: A division commander wants his eyes and ears forward to give him situational awareness before he maneuvers. Which unit fits that role?
options: A tank unit
A mechanized infantry unit
Cavalry
A fire support vehicle section
explanation: Page 53 describes cavalry as the commander's eyes and ears.

prompt: A staff lists cavalry organizations: squadron/battalion, troop/company, air cavalry squadron, and separate troop/company. How many basic designs does the lesson give for cavalry?
options: Three
Five
Four
Two
explanation: Page 55 lists four basic cavalry designs.

prompt: A brigade commander wants a unit that can hold part of the front thinly so he can conserve combat power for engagement where he wishes. Which cavalry role does this describe?
options: Main effort
Counterattack force
Economy of force
Rear area security only
explanation: Page 54 describes cavalry as an economy of force that lets the commander conserve combat power.

prompt: A commander assigns a unit to neutralize enemy forces by fire, maneuver and shock effect in coordination with other units. Which armor sub-component is this?
options: Tank operations
Cavalry operations
Mechanized infantry operations
Fire support operations
explanation: Pages 17 and 63 give this as the tank mission.

prompt: A tank company commander reviews the organization of one platoon. Which description matches the lesson?
options: Three tanks, each crewed by a commander and a driver only
Five tanks, each crewed by four soldiers including a loader
Two tanks, each crewed by a gunner and a driver only
Four tanks, each crewed by a tank commander, a gunner and a driver
explanation: Page 65 shows a platoon of four tanks, each with commander, gunner and driver.

prompt: A tank company will attack at night. Which capability does the lesson give tanks for night fighting?
options: Tanks need infantry to light the targets before they can fire accurately
Thermal sights greatly enhance the night fighting capability of the combined arms team
Tanks cannot fight at night and must wait for daylight to engage
Night fighting is done only by dismounted infantry using night vision goggles
explanation: Page 66 says tanks use thermal sights to greatly enhance night fighting.

prompt: A mechanized infantry company commander is planning where his troops get off their vehicles. Which options does the lesson list?
options: Only on the objective
Only before the line of departure
Only after the enemy has withdrawn
On, before or after the objective
explanation: Page 69 lists where to dismount troops: on, before or after the objective.

prompt: A staff reviews planning considerations for armor units. Which statement matches the lesson?
options: Mechanized infantry and cavalry are the best choice against enemy tank units, while tanks should avoid other tanks
Tanks cannot be used against other tanks, so tank units are left to mechanized infantry
Mechanized infantry and cavalry cannot be used against tank units, but tanks can be used against other tanks or any enemy armored vehicle
All three armor units can be used equally against enemy tank units with no special planning
explanation: Pages 69-71 list this consideration for each unit.

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: A battalion receives a wheeled APC acquired in 2024 under the Horizon 2 Project, with a crew of 3 and 7 passengers. Which vehicle is it?
options: Simba Fighting Vehicle
Commando V-150S
Guarani 6x6 wheeled APC
M113A2 APC
explanation: Page 83 lists these specifications for the Guarani 6x6 wheeled APC.

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: An internal security unit wants a wheeled AFV designed for internal security operations, with a fully enclosed one-man turret and run-flat tires. Which vehicle?
options: Sabrah Light Tank ASCOD II
Commando V-150S
M113A2 APC
Fire Support Vehicle
explanation: Page 79 describes the Commando V-150S with these characteristics.

category: Major Equipment of the Armor Division
prompt: Which vehicle in the lesson is the light tank armed with a 105 mm gun and crewed by three?
options: Sabrah Light Tank ASCOD II
Fire Support Vehicle
Simba Fighting Vehicle
M113A2 IFV Unmanned Turret System
explanation: Page 82 gives the Sabrah specification: 105 mm main armament and a crew of 3.
